source.file: full.stl (Autodesk ATF export, binary STL with per-face colour)
source.colourEncoding: face attribute bits 0-4 R, 5-9 G, 10-14 B (x8); bit 15 = 0

frame.origin: ground plane (soles at Z = 0), midway between the hip-yaw axes (Y), on the leg pitch-axis line (X)
frame.fromSTL: X = -(y_stl - -17.0684), Y = x_stl - -0.0074, Z = z_stl - -345.9205, then the per-part rectification
frame.toThreeJs: Y-up renderers: (x3, y3, z3) = (Y, Z, X). A camera on +z3 then sees the front of the robot, its left on screen-right.

binary.positions: per part: Int16 x,y,z interleaved (mesh.vertexCount * 3 values) at mesh.vertexByteOffset; mm = int16 * quant.scale + quant.offset[axis]
binary.indices: per part: Uint16 ("u16") or Uint32 ("u32") triangle list at mesh.indexByteOffset, mesh.indexCount values, counter-clockwise = outward
binary.groups: mesh.groups[]: {material, start, count} counted in TRIANGLES within the part; faces are sorted by material
binary.alignment: every block starts on a 4-byte boundary
binary.normals: not stored; compute flat (face) normals in the browser (biped-loader.js does this)
binary.decimation: per part: vertex clustering on a mesh.cell mm grid with quadric-error representatives (Lindstrom 2000)

overall.note: height = ground to the top of the Raspberry Pi ports; width x depth = the torso box

legs.note: thighLength/shinLength = axis-to-axis; legLength = hip-pitch axis to ground; thigh and shin are the same printed part

foot.note: length along X (toe forward); height includes the ankle clevis; soleArea = flat contact face of one foot

repo.note: label.py in the biped repo sets IDs 1-8 and home = 120 deg (middle of 0-240)

printed.note: solid CAD volume of the 10 printed parts; printed mass depends on infill, so no mass is claimed

kinematics.chain: torso -> hip_yaw -> hip (yoke) -> hip_pitch -> thigh -> knee -> shin -> ankle -> foot, per side
kinematics.angleSign: right-hand rule about the joint axis. Pitch axes are +Y (robot's left): a positive angle swings the link below the joint BACKWARD (knee flexion > 0, hip flexion < 0, toes-up ankle < 0). Hip yaw about +Z: positive turns the toes to the robot's left.
kinematics.restPose: all joints 0 = legs straight, soles flat on Z = 0; the geometry in biped.bin is already in this pose
kinematics.footFlat: all pitch axes are parallel, so the sole stays level when ankle = -(hip_pitch + knee)
kinematics.servoMapping: which servo ID (1-8) drives which joint, and each servo's direction, are not in the CAD or the repo; the angle sign here is ours

rectification.why: The exported CAD assembly is not fully mated. Right leg (Y<0): mated, but posed with hip yaw 1.96 deg and ankle pitch 0.98 deg. Left leg (Y>0): axis-aligned, but its parts slid along Z (3.75 mm gap under the hip-yaw horn; foot 11.3 mm off its ankle axis). Rest pose written here = right leg with those two joints set to 0; left leg = the same arrangement about the left hip axis (pure translations). Electronics, torso and hip-yaw servos are untouched.
rectification.perPartNote: 4x4 row-major matrices mapping original STL coordinates to the web frame for the parts that were moved; every other part uses toWeb
